claims.text: Controlled aging can form fine, coherent nanoprecipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Controlled aging that forms coherent nanoprecipitates will improve the alloy's strength–plasticity combination relative to the as-cast or solution-treated state.
The initial as-cast or solution-treated alloy has a homogeneous microstructure without preexisting fine precipitates.
Aging below the recrystallization threshold for a tuned duration will produce well-dispersed, fine, coherent nanoprecipitates.
A sufficiently low aging temperature and optimized hold time will maintain precipitate coherency and avoid coarsening or incoherency.
The aging treatment will form uniformly dispersed nanoscale coherent precipitates that interact with dislocations.
The nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength through precipitation strengthening.
The nanoprecipitates promote strain hardening, potentially through precipitate-induced twinning or dislocation pile-up.
Precipitate-promoted strain hardening will contribute to improved plasticity.
The aged alloy will exhibit both higher yield strength and greater plastic strain before failure than the unaged baseline.
The intervention requires an alloy with sufficient compositional complexity to form coherent precipitates.
Inappropriate aging temperatures or durations may prevent the predicted beneficial outcome.
